title: ABO Blood Group System: Basics and Forward/Reverse Typing
summary: One-paragraph overview used in cards and search results: the ABO system is defined by A and B antigens on red cells and the matching isohemagglutinins in plasma; forward (cell) and reverse (serum) typing must agree before blood is issued.
objectives: Explain the biochemical basis of A and B antigens on red cells.
Perform and interpret forward and reverse ABO typing.
Predict ABO group from secretor status and genotype.

highYield: Group A red cells carry A antigen; plasma contains anti-B.
Group O red cells carry neither A nor B antigen; plasma contains anti-A and anti-B.
Discrepancy between forward and reverse typing must be resolved before issuing blood.
quickReview.mnemonic: O has nO antigens and bOth antibodies.

deepStudy.introduction: ABO typing is the single most important pretransfusion test. A and B antigens are carbohydrate structures added to the H antigen by glycosyltransferases; individuals who lack a given antigen usually make a corresponding IgM antibody (isohemagglutinin) in the first months of life, likely in response to environmental antigens.

sections.heading: Molecular basis
sections.body: The ABO gene on chromosome 9 encodes a glycosyltransferase. The A allele adds N-acetylgalactosamine to the H substance; the B allele adds D-galactose; the O allele produces a non-functional enzyme so the H antigen remains unmodified.

sections.heading: Forward and reverse typing
sections.body: Forward typing tests patient red cells with known anti-A and anti-B. Reverse typing tests patient serum/plasma with known A1 and B reagent cells. Both must agree; newborns and the elderly may have weak or absent reverse reactions.

deepStudy.clinicalSignificance: ABO-incompatible transfusion causes immediate intravascular hemolysis and can be fatal; ABO-incompatible organ transplantation must be avoided except in approved protocols.
deepStudy.labInterpretation: A forward/reverse discrepancy must be investigated (recent transfusion, newborn, hypogammaglobulinemia, mixed-field reaction, or extra/missing antibodies) before any component is issued. Reference intervals for related titers vary by laboratory, method, age, sex, and population; verify against your local laboratory.
examTraps: Reverse typing in newborns is weak or absent because antibodies are IgG maternal or not yet produced; do not rely on reverse typing alone.
Group O plasma contains both anti-A and anti-B; it is the universal RBC donor, NOT the universal plasma donor.

memoryHooks.text: O has nO antigens and bOth antibodies.
memoryHooks.funny: Meow: 'nO antigens, bOth antibodies — like a cat with no manners and all the opinions.'
